result.benchmark_cells: Descriptive, no refit, native genuine only. One-person head AUC (CLIP pooled / CLIP patch / DINOv3): FRLL-Morphs StyleGAN 0.72 [0.67, 0.77] / 0.64 / 0.75; corrected MAD22 MIPGAN-I 0.73 [0.67, 0.78] / 0.48 / 0.45; corrected MAD22 MIPGAN-II 0.64 [0.58, 0.69] / 0.38 / 0.49. Two-person head, CLIP pooled: 0.75 / 0.70 / 0.64. With softening removed, the CLIP pooled one-person head gives 0.67 / 0.62 / 0.53. The neutral-only genuine column is higher in every row (for example 0.81). Per the rule on FRLL neutral-plus-smiling pairs, no conclusion is drawn from that.
caveats: The verdict 'idea works' comes from the pre-registered rule: on CLIP pooled the one-person head reaches 0.80 for x3 vs x1, exceeds the image-statistic floor by 0.20 and flags 4.4% of softened photos. It is NOT evidence of second-identity reading. The registered latent-averageness qualifier fires for every feature: against spread-matched one-identity renders the same heads score 0.44 to 0.48, they rank those one-identity renders above reconstructions at 0.84 to 0.88, and the latent distance-to-mean statistic alone gives 1.00. What the one-person head catches in GAN morphs is that a midpoint latent lies closer to the mean code.
The registered floor contains image statistics only; latent distance cannot be computed from an image and was registered as reported-not-floor. Had it counted, every head would sit below the floor.
Against the same-person-mix reference (x3 vs x2) the one-person head reaches only 0.57 to 0.63, and the latent statistic alone gives 0.95 there.

Set G is small (64 blocks, about +-0.04 on the primary AUC). Its camera photos x0 are in a different frame and resolution from the renders, so x0->x1 mixes the generator with frame, background and resolution changes.

Mirror self-morphs, graded mixing and MIPGAN one-person images do not exist for this family. G-morph potency (verification against both contributors) was not checked, and the H3 potency gate failed earlier (48%).
The registered DINOv3 mean patch token is identical to DINOv3 pooled (timm averages patch tokens), so DINOv3 counts as one feature.

Deviations from the pre-registration: GPU feature extraction took about 67 minutes of wall time on the shared GB10 (registered budget 1 hour; peak memory 1.7 GB). The roughly 20 s first pass ran as a 5th process while extraction used 4.
Regularisation C was mostly chosen at 0.001 to 0.01, and 0.001 is the edge of the grid.
Cross-set cosine intervals are bootstrap percentiles of a downward-biased statistic. Q4 (d) on set H is in-sample and is not reported.

What the one-person heads learn is blending of two captures, not a second identity. They score mirror self-morphs like two-person morphs (xm vs x3 0.44 to 0.60) and only partly separate same-person morphs (0.64 to 0.80). Under the proposed class definitions they would flag single-subject manipulations as attacks.

The registered softened-genuine sets (FRLL and MAD22 E7, OpenCV family) are mild. On the hosts' own shrink-and-enlarge copies at the stronger registered strength (amendment 1, descriptive), the CLIP class-token one-person head flags 27.5% [21.4,34.2], which is above the 15% bar that applies to the registered sets. It also flags 22% of SMDD stored-small copies. Projecting out the host-softening direction brings these to 4.5% and 3.2% with no AUC loss. CLIP mean and DINOv3 stay at or below 7.5%.

Geometry mismatch: x1 is warped toward the same person's shape, x3 toward the mean with another person's shape. The matched-geometry AF0 halves test (0.970 to 0.999, floor 0.831) uses other persons and the OpenCV engine only.

The floor is the best single statistic, picked post hoc. A head on all 27 statistics (amendment 2) reaches 0.853 on x1 vs x3 but is a softness detector (flags 70% of FRLL E7; ranks softened one-person images above morphs).

Amendments 1 and 2 were written after I had seen the CLIP results and a code-path test (one C, 200 draws), but before any of their own numbers. The new sets are descriptive and the registered readings are unchanged.

The bootstrap intervals cover person sampling only, not head fitting. The chosen regularisation sits at the grid edge for the CLIP mean one-person head (C=0.001), the statistics control and the two-person heads (C=1).

Not tested: whether the heads read blending in the face or in the surround (no blanked rerun); WebMorph or AMSL as training engines. FaceMorpher results are descriptive. Benchmark frames use a different alignment from the training frames, and the benchmark morphs are AF0's 600-image subsample.

The SMDD softening direction passes 256 px and 80 px images through each backbone's own resize (standard preprocessing only; no image written). The host-softening direction covers 200 of the 536 hosts.

The machine was heavily shared. One DINOv3 smoke run hit a CUDA allocation error and succeeded on retry. CLIP was re-extracted (the class token is not in any cache); its mean patch token was verified against AF0's cache. No git operations, no WCSS, no spending.

result.corrected_wording:
Landmark morphs, OpenCV-style engine, frozen features, 536 FRGC and colorFERET hosts. AUC = area under the ROC curve.

What holds. A linear head trained only on one-person images (same-person morphs and mirror self-morphs against the warp-only image of the same host) ranks two-person morphs of held-out persons above their warp-only images: AUC 0.998 (CLIP class token), 0.985 to 0.987 (CLIP mean patch token), 0.93 (DINOv3 mean patch token). This reproduces with independent code and folds, across the two databases, on unseen persons, and with matched warp geometry. No leakage, no FRLL person in a fit, registration in order.

What it is not. It is not a second-identity signal (mirror self-morphs score like two-person morphs), and it is no better than training on two-person morphs directly. The within-host paired loss is not what makes it work: an ordinary unpaired logistic regression on the same one-person images gives 0.999 to 1.000 for all three features.

Where the registered result does not survive.
1. The separation sits mainly outside the face. With only the surround visible the heads keep 0.92 to 0.99. With only the face hull visible they fall to 0.62 to 0.71, below the best single simple statistic (0.89). Refitted on face-only images the registered paired head reaches 0.86 to 0.91, which does not exceed that statistic. So on full frames the head mostly detects the double-exposed surround that this whole-frame blending engine produces. Consistent with that, it is weaker on morphs with a spliced face (FRLL-Morphs AMSL 0.76 to 0.88; approved Poisson set (H1) 0.77 to 0.89).
2. The CLIP class-token head flags 27.5% [21.4, 34.2] of the hosts' own softened photos at the stronger registered strength (bar 15%). It passes on the registered sets, one of which is almost unsoftened.
3. The margin over simple statistics depends on the floor: 0.10 to 0.11 over the registered pooled single statistic for CLIP, but 0.03 to 0.04 over a logistic regression on the 27 statistics trained on the same one-person images (0.956), and nothing for DINOv3.

What remains open in the idea's favour. A face-region signal learned from one-person images does appear with an unpaired head refitted on face-only images: 0.95 to 0.98, which is 0.06 to 0.09 above the best single statistic and equal to a two-person-trained head. This variant was chosen after seeing results, is not registered, and its reaction to softened photos is untested.

Reading: by the registration as written the family reads "idea works" (2 of 3 features). After the surround and softened-host attacks the supportable statement is "mixed": learning from one-person morphs transfers to two-person morphs of a whole-frame blending tool, mainly as a detector of double exposure outside the face; a face-region morph signal beyond simple statistics is not shown with the registered head.
what_would_settle_it: Register a face-region version of the author's test as primary: surround blanked to constant grey in every rung (existing blanked copies), unpaired logistic head, a fresh person split, with the fixed reading unchanged. Include the softened-photo leg: existing softened copies of the hosts, blanked the same way (needs only constant-colour blanking of existing softened images).

Build the one-person ladder (warp-only, mirror self-morph, same-person morph, two-person morph) with the approved Poisson warp script, where the surround comes from the host photo only, and repeat Q3 there. If the one-person head still separates at 0.75 or more above the floor, the signal is face blending; if it collapses, it was surround double exposure.
Score the benchmark cells with the surround blanked under the benchmark alignment, in particular FRLL-Morphs AMSL and WebMorph, with one-person and two-person heads side by side.

Train with softened one-person images as extra negatives (the author's 'softness is not blending') and re-measure the CLIP class-token flag rate on the hosts' own softened photos at both strengths; compare with the projection of the host-softening direction (which already gives 4%).

Fix the floor before the next run as a logistic regression on the 27 simple statistics trained on the same images and reported per database, and state the margin as a ratio of error (1 minus AUC) rather than an AUC difference, because a 0.05 gap cannot be reached above 0.95.

Replace the within-host paired loss by an ordinary unpaired head (or add a between-host term) in the registration, and confirm on the 663 unseen persons of the alpha-field probe (AF0) once one-person morphs or blanked halves exist for them.

result.corrected_wording:
Signal isolation by paired differences (PD1), diffusion-autoencoder (DiffAE) family. A linear head trained only on one-person images (same-person DiffAE mix against the reconstruction of the same photo) separates two-person DiffAE morphs from reconstructions on held-out persons at AUC 0.95 [0.92, 0.97] on frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 pooled features (0.88 to 0.92 on the other two feature sets), 0.78 to 0.95 from one photo database to the other, and 0.89 on FRLL at 256 px; 2 to 4% of softened genuine photos are flagged. The registered reading "works" is met as written and every number reproduces.

What transfers is a render-texture trace of DiffAE mixing at equal render settings, not a morph-specific signal:
1. A head on 26 simple image statistics trained the same one-person way reaches 0.947; the excess of the feature head over it is +0.00 [-0.03, +0.04]. The registered +0.18 is against a single statistic only.
2. The head ranks same-person mixes and mirror mixes above two-person morphs (0.29 and 0.20). Under the three-category definitions it detects a single-subject manipulation.
3. It reacts to decoding steps without any mixing: the 100-step reconstruction of a photo outscores its 20-step reconstruction in 197 of 204 FRLL photos, 35% of them are flagged at the threshold that flags 5% of 20-step reconstructions, and a 20-step morph against 100-step reconstructions gives 0.73. The two-person-trained head behaves the same.
4. With the face blanked it still reaches 0.94.
5. For morph against genuine photo on the training hosts it stays below one statistic (0.88 against 0.91 for file size, 0.955 for median absolute Laplacian).

Benchmark cells are descriptive and not robust: MorDIFF 0.61 to 0.68 and the DiM families 0.61 to 0.99 depending on the regularisation strength (the reported values are the setting chosen by a tie-break), and published MorDIFF morphs separate from 100-step one-photo reconstructions at only 0.60 [0.52, 0.70]. "Second identity is a consistent direction" holds on the pooled set but is confounded with session in FERET and is 0.74 to 0.79 on FRGC. The softening control is uninformative here because DiffAE mixes carry more fine detail than reconstructions, not less.
what_would_settle_it: Render the training hosts' reconstructions (and a subset of mixes) at several decoding step counts (20, 50, 100) with the pinned DiffAE, then refit the one-person head with step count crossed between positives and negatives and re-apply the 0.75 / +0.05 / 15% rule with 'more steps, no mixing' as the false-alarm pool. A one-photo control that uses the mixing arithmetic without a second image: decode a photo's semantic code with a stochastic code that no longer matches it (for example slerp with an independent Gaussian draw), or repair the identical-inputs path of the identical-and-mirrored-inputs check (AD1b), which currently returns NaN. Register the simple-statistic floor as a combined head (the 26 native-size statistics in /mnt/t7/smad_next/PD1/diffusion/verify/v2_stats.py) for all three families and re-apply the +0.05 rule; add a matched test in which morphs and reconstructions are paired on file size and spectral band energies.

DiM-pipeline reconstructions and same-person DiM mixes of FRLL photos (DiM A, Fast-DiM, Greedy-DiM), so the DiM benchmark cells can be split into pipeline and mixing steps; depends on the DiM code running (ladder on DiM and Greedy-DiM, AD2).
The decoding step count of the published MorDIFF set (authors' code or the authors themselves) to fix which reconstruction is the right control for that cell.

result.answer:
No shared mixing direction, and no transfer: a one-person head trained on two morph families did not detect two-person morphs of the third. All 9 registered held-out cells (3 families x 3 features) read "fails", so the plain answer is no. With frozen CLIP ViT-L/14 pooled, CLIP mean patch and DINOv3 ViT-L/16 features and linear heads, a detector trained on one-person morphs of several pipelines would not be expected to detect two-person morphs of an unseen pipeline.

- **Two-person heads fail too.** Heads trained on two-person morphs of two families give 0.38 to 0.69 on the held-out family, so the failure is not caused by training on one-person images.
- **Softness is not the cause.** The registered softened genuine sets are flagged at 3.9 to 8.8%.
- **The code and features are sound.** The same heads fitted inside each family reproduce the families' own numbers: landmark 1.00/0.99/0.95, diffusion 0.95/0.88/0.91, GAN 0.81/0.78/0.79.
- **Each family's one-person signal is specific to its pipeline.** Landmark reads double exposure, mostly in the surround. Diffusion reads render texture. GAN reads the latent code pulled toward the mean. The GAN direction is partly opposed to the other two.

**Verdicts used.** Landmark and diffusion use the verified "mixed". GAN had no delivered verification (a partial sceptic run exists on disk), so the owner's "idea works" stands, with its own latent-averageness qualifier fired.

**Process.**
- Pre-registration was written before any number. Amendment 1 (before any number): the diffusion CLIP cache failed my 1e-3 equality check (0.0031, made with TF32 off), so all diffusion images were re-extracted with the common code.
- Amendment 2 is post hoc, written after the CLIP results: pairwise single-family transfer and probes of the mean-direction heads.
- An 8-image smoke test ran before every command. An analysis code-path test (fewer draws) ran after registration; its head point estimates equal the full run's.
- Compute: about 9 GPU-minutes, peak 1.72 GB; at most 2 CPU processes with nice 10. No git, cluster or spending.
- The pre-registration, result and README (`README.md` per `DOCUMENTATION.md`, current as of 21:21) are written. No independent review of this step has run.
result.cosines_between_families:
The one-person mixing step (x1 to x2) is not shared by any pair of families. Values are cross-fitted cosines in z-space over 200 person-half splits, for CLIP pooled / CLIP patch / DINOv3:

| Step | Landmark vs diffusion | Landmark vs GAN | Diffusion vs GAN |
|---|---|---|---|
| One-person mixing | 0.44 / 0.37 / 0.15 | -0.04 / -0.15 / -0.13 | -0.27 / -0.37 / -0.45 |
| Whole morph (x1 to x3) | 0.38 / 0.37 / 0.23 | -0.16 / -0.11 / -0.13 | -0.16 / -0.09 / -0.25 |
| Pipeline (x0 to x1) | 0.08 / -0.18 / -0.03 | 0.02 / 0.08 / 0.09 | 0.59 / 0.30 / 0.30 |

- **Reading.** All 9 mixing pairs read "not shared", including after disattenuation (landmark vs diffusion 0.45/0.39/0.16). The registered reading is "no shared mixing direction" in all three features.
- **Reliabilities are high enough for that reading.** Split-half reliability of the mixing directions is 0.94 to 0.99 for landmark and diffusion, and 0.67 to 0.83 for GAN.
- **Whole morph and pipeline also read "no shared direction".** The only "shared" pipeline pair is diffusion vs GAN in CLIP pooled (0.59): generator reconstruction is a common direction.
- **Secondary L2 space gives the same picture.** Only landmark vs diffusion mixing in CLIP pooled reaches 0.50.
- **The mixing directions are not softness.** Cosines with SMDD softening are -0.23 to 0.23.
- **The GAN mixing direction is GAN latent spread.** It aligns with the one-identity latent-spread direction (0.56 to 0.73), while diffusion mixing is opposed to it (-0.28 to -0.51).
- **The GAN pipeline step looks like landmark mixing.** Camera photo to GAN render aligns with landmark mixing at 0.32 to 0.59.
result.leave_one_family_out:
Heads were fitted on two families, with every person of the held-out family removed from training, and scored on all hosts of the third. AUC is x1 vs x3 with a 95% person bootstrap, for CLIP pooled / CLIP patch / DINOv3.

| Held out | Training hosts | One-person head | Floor | Two-person head | Flag rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Landmark (536 hosts) | diffusion 124, GAN 40 | 0.432 [0.386, 0.482] / 0.676 / 0.522 | 0.886 | 0.48 / 0.69 / 0.56 | 4.4 to 5.4% |
| Diffusion (516 hosts) | landmark 291, GAN 56 | 0.555 [0.499, 0.613] / 0.559 / 0.506 | 0.773 | 0.59 / 0.68 / 0.59 | 5.9 to 8.3% |
| GAN (256 hosts) | landmark 399, diffusion 316 | 0.383 [0.298, 0.475] / 0.300 / 0.325 | 0.601 | 0.44 / 0.41 / 0.38 | 3.9 to 5.4% |

- **Every cell fails.** Excess over the floor is -0.45 to -0.21 with all intervals below 0.
- **Transfer gap against the in-family head on the same features** is -0.57 to -0.32 for landmark, -0.41 to -0.32 for diffusion and -0.48 to -0.43 for GAN.
- **Robust to the head recipe.** All five C values fail; the best is the smallest C on landmark, 0.78 / 0.81, still below the floor. No person purge, landmark x2-only positives and unweighted families: all 27 sensitivity cells fail.
- **What the heads read on GAN.** Heads trained on landmark and diffusion score GAN renders whose latent is nearer the mean lower (set H x1 vs x3 0.24 to 0.38; x1 vs x1s 0.25 to 0.43), and separate camera photos from renders at 0.95.
- **What the heads read on diffusion.** They read the DiffAE pipeline (photo vs reconstruction 0.65 to 0.75) more than DiffAE mixing (0.38 to 0.49).
- **Post hoc, pairwise.** Diffusion to landmark gives 0.61 to 0.91, and the unfitted mean direction 0.976 on CLIP pooled. GAN to landmark is opposed (0.10 to 0.47). Landmark to diffusion is 0.62 to 0.74; every pair involving GAN is at most 0.51.
- **The one transferring direction reads the surround.** On landmark it gives surround only 0.95 and face only 0.54, and scores mirror self-morphs like morphs (0.44).
result.largest_threat:
Family is confounded with frame, resolution and photo source:
- landmark: 512 px aligned frames;
- diffusion: 256 px DiffAE crops;
- GAN: 1,024 px renders, with camera photos in a third frame.

Each family's one-person signal was also found to be largely a pipeline artefact: by the verifiers for landmark (surround double exposure) and diffusion (render texture and decoding steps), and by the owner's registered qualifier for GAN (latent averageness).

So the negative shows that these pipeline artefacts do not transfer. It does not show that a blending signal confined to the face could not transfer once all pipelines run on the same host photos in one frame, with the surround blanked. That test needs new generation, which is the author's call.

Some shared component does exist between landmark and diffusion: cosines 0.15 to 0.44, and the post hoc diffusion mean direction transfers to landmark at 0.976. But it reads the landmark surround (face only 0.54), so it is not evidence of a shared face-morph signal.

Smaller threats: only three families; frozen features with linear heads only, so a fine-tuned network was not tested; and small purged GAN training sets (40 and 56 hosts). The no-purge run with 256 GAN hosts gives the same readings.
